ResourceHeader.Description: IBEX-Hi Release 18 fourteen-year combined Solar Ecliptic hydrogen ENA maps from omnidirectional observations. The mono designation identifies mono-energy Compton-Getting-corrected maps. Compton-Getting correction accounts for spacecraft motion relative to the arriving ENAs. The product identifier and detailed source description designate survival-probability-corrected fluxes, scaled from the IBEX observing location near 1 AU to approximately 100 AU. The Release 18 source metadata describes observations for 2009-2022. Each map has 60 longitude bins by 30 latitude bins at six-degree spacing. The channel 2-6 nominal mono-energies are 0.71, 1.11, 1.74, 2.73, and 4.29 keV; the corresponding instrument-channel FWHM ranges are 0.52-0.95, 0.84-1.55, 1.36-2.50, 1.99-3.75, and 3.13-6.00 keV. The CDF variables described here include a dimensionless fit-parameter map (Parm), differential hydrogen ENA flux, signal-to-noise ratio, and flux variance, together with time, map, coordinate and orbit support variables and virtual CDAWeb _plasma alternate views. The source ASCII filename pattern is hvset_tabular_omni_cg_2009-2022\hv60.hide-trp-mono_80-M-V. The CDAWeb ProductKey is IBEX_H3_ENA_HI_R18_CG_SP_OMNI_MONO_14YR.

NumericalData.Caveats: Compton-Getting correction for spacecraft motion is applied. This record follows the CG/SP/MONO product identifier and detailed source description, which designate survival-probability-corrected mono-energy data scaled from near 1 AU to approximately 100 AU. This product contains one combined fourteen-year map, not a time series resolved within that interval. The _plasma variables are virtual CDAWeb X/Y alternate views of their corresponding source arrays. The listed nominal energies identify the mono-energy samples; the quoted FWHM energy ranges describe the associated instrument channels, not an additional bandwidth of the mono-energy samples. The source metadata identifies Parm only as a dimensionless fit parameter and does not specify the fitted model or a more detailed physical definition.
